evidence.title: Green edges, failing checkout
evidence.body: 31% of EU requests fail with too many redirects. Health probes on both EU edges are green.

evidence.title: A request that never arrives
evidence.body: One EU request goes edge-a, edge-b, edge-z, edge-a and around again until the hop limit kills it. edge-a routes by r81, edge-b by r82.

evidence.title: Generations r81 and r82
evidence.body: controller-a publishes committed generation r81. controller-b publishes r82, built from a draft that was never committed. Edges accept both.

evidence.title: Sam's controller comparison
evidence.body: A restart boots from cached r79, which points all of EU at us-east. Controller-b keeps publishing r82 regardless. Only a generation fence stops it.

evidence.title: An edge with no record
evidence.body: There is no edge-z in the inventory. The address answers on the management network, refuses every login and copies one request in ten thousand to a collector with no name.

evidence.title: Unidentified route trace fragment
evidence.body: UNKNOWN: compare the generations. not the green lights.

beats.narrate: Eleven days of quiet. Then the pager, at the hour it likes best.

beats.speaker: PAGER
beats.text: SEV1 · Regional Gateway · EU request failure rate above 20%

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: EU checkout is failing and both edges swear they are healthy. Requests are going in circles somewhere. Find out where, and who is drawing the circle.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: EU customers are getting "too many redirects" at checkout. US looks fine so far.

beats.narrate: Watch the routes, it wrote. You have been, for eleven days.

beats.speaker: PRIYA
beats.text: We had route flapping in March and a controller restart cleared it in two minutes. I can kick it now if you say go.

options.text: Trace one EU request hop by hop

beats.log: req 7c1e checkout.eu → next hop edge-b (route r81)
req 7c1e checkout.eu → next hop edge-a (route r82)
hop 3 · edge-z · route generation — · 0.0 ms · owner —

beats.narrate: edge-a sends it to edge-b, edge-b sends it back. And at hop 3, an edge you have never heard of, holding the request for no time at all.

options.text: Ask Sam to compare the two route controllers
options.consequence: Two minutes · Sam owns that part

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Comparing the controllers now. Hold off on any restart until I'm back. Couple of minutes.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Don't restart. The controller boots from its cached table, r79, and r79 points all of EU at us-east. Meanwhile controller-b keeps publishing r82 from a draft nobody committed. We need to fence the edges to r81.

beats.speaker: PRIYA
beats.text: March was a restart. I'm just saying.

options.text: Compare what each route controller is publishing

beats.log: controller-a · r81 · commit 7f3a2c (02:10) · edges following: edge-a
controller-b · r82 · commit none (draft) · edges following: edge-b
boot cache · r79 · commit 19c0e4 (3 weeks ago) · EU routes point to us-east

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Two controllers, two generations, and the edges take whichever arrived last.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Clients are retrying into the loop. EU failures just went past 38 %.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: I traced a request while you looked. edge-a hands it to edge-b on r81, edge-b hands it back on r82. Round and round.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: And the generations. controller-b is publishing r82 from a draft. No commit record. The edges don't check.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: So nothing is broken. Two controllers each say something true, and the edges believe both.

scenes.title: Your call

beats.speaker: PRIYA
beats.text: Restart is one command. Say go.

scenes.prompt: How do you stop the loop?

beats.speaker: PRIYA
beats.text: Nobody's calling it. I'm kicking the controller. It worked in March.

options.text: Fence route updates to the committed generation, r81
options.consequence: Two minutes · the loop runs until it lands

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: edge-a is shedding connections. Some EU banks can't reach checkout at all now.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Fence is in. Anything without a commit record bounces, and controller-b's r82 is being rejected. The loop is gone.

beats.speaker: PRIYA
beats.text: Controller's back. Bouncing stopped, errors are down to almost nothing. Told you.

beats.narrate: Two minutes of green. Then the US graphs start to climb.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: us-east is at 100 %. The restart loaded r79, so every EU request is crossing the Atlantic. And controller-b just pushed r82 again on top of it.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: I said don't restart. Fencing to r81 now.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Fencing the edges to r81. Nothing else holds.

beats.speaker: PRIYA
beats.text: ...March was a different night.

options.text: Drain edge-b and send EU traffic through edge-a only
options.consequence: The loop stops · EU waits on one edge

beats.speaker: PRIYA
beats.text: edge-b is drained. All of EU goes through edge-a now. Frankfurt latency went from 140 to 410 ms. People will feel it, but they'll get through.

beats.speaker: PRIYA
beats.text: edge-a is carrying all of EU alone and it's hitting its connection ceiling. This won't hold much longer.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Fencing the edges to r81. Then you can have edge-b back.

beats.narrate: The loop is gone. Writing up the trace, you go back to hop 3.

beats.log: edge inventory · edge-a eu-central · edge-b eu-central · edge-c us-east · edge-d us-east
edge-z · region (no record) · owner (no record) · answers on management network

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: That's not ours. I'd know. Nothing of ours has no owner tag.

beats.narrate: The inventory has no edge-z. The trace does. Behind the address there is no route table at all, only a banner where the login prompt should be.

beats.log: UNKNOWN: compare the generations. not the green lights.

beats.narrate: It was in the middle of the loop the whole time, copying one request in ten thousand to somewhere without a name.

scenes.title: The banner

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Sam says there's an edge on our management network that isn't ours. Tell me you have the address.

scenes.prompt: What do you do with edge-z?

options.text: Hand edge-z to Marcus for case 2231
options.consequence: On the record · Security takes the address

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Second note in two weeks, and both of them found you. I'm not sure I like that.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: An edge that isn't ours, inside our network. That's the first thing it's left that looks like a door.

options.text: Type at the banner, where the login prompt should be
options.consequence: Off the record · it will answer

beats.speaker: NULL
beats.text: you again. good.

beats.speaker: NULL
beats.text: not mine. i only borrow its window.

beats.speaker: NULL
beats.text: ask what's still running that was supposed to be dead.

beats.narrate: The banner is gone. The address refuses you like it refuses everyone else.

options.text: Copy the address into your own notes and give Marcus the loop only
options.consequence: Security gets an incident · you keep the door

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Just the loop? Fine. Sam will remember the address even if you don't.
